I farm here in Ruvuma like my father did. I have almost two hectares of maize on my own land, and the rains here are good most years, so I do not need to buy much. I cannot read the writing on those fertilizer bags, and one bag costs too much money for me — I will put manure from my few goats and chickens on the part near the house, and use the seed I kept from last year's harvest like my neighbors do. I will weed with my wife and my older children, and when planting and harvest come I will call two men from the village to help me for a few days because the plot is big for one family.
